title: A spectral representation for the nonabelian Toda chain
statement: For the matrix chain \(\dot A_s=B_s-B_{s-1}\), \(\dot B_s=B_sA_{s+1}-A_sB_s\), construct a spectral auxiliary linear system whose compatibility is exactly these equations. Finite periodic chains give a concrete algebraic setting; infinite-chain spectral statements require additional decay and domain conditions.
status: As of 10 November 2026: resolved. The difference-operator pair \(\mathcal L=E^{-1}+A+BE\), \(\mathcal M=BE\) verifies the compatibility directly. Subsequent nonabelian Toda solution theory is traced to Krichever 1981 by \citet[\S1 and \S9]{takebezabrodin2025multicomponent}. The earlier scalar periodic-Toda involution problem GP-1975-05 concerns a different assertion and is not merged with this matrix Lax-representation question.

title: Anisotropic regular factorization for the spin-one density: literal and corrected versions
statement: Find a parameter family of analytic regular difference-form R-matrices whose Hamiltonian specializes to the rotationally invariant spin-one density printed on P000818. The literal density is \(X^2-2X\), with \([S^a,S^b]=\varepsilon_{abc}S^c\) and \(X=\sum_aS^a\otimes S^a\). Separately, the identified corrected historical problem concerns anisotropic deformations of \(J\cdot J-(J\cdot J)^2\) for Hermitian spin-one generators.
status: As of 10 November 2026: the literal regular difference-form extension is excluded by the exact cubic obstruction proved in this chapter. The nearby correctly normalized anisotropic model was published by \citet{zamolodchikovfateev1980spin} in 1980; its explicit relation to the isotropic density is checked in \citet[Sec.~5]{bytsko2003xxz}. This is a closed negative literal result plus a solved corrected construction, not a manufactured open remainder.

title: The finite periodic XYZ spectral problem
statement: For real \(J_1,J_2,J_3\) and \(N\ge2\), diagonalize \(H=\sum_{n=1}^N\sum_{a=1}^3J_a\sigma_n^a\sigma_{n+1}^a\) on \((\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}\), with periodic boundaries, by an integrable description uniform in N. Multiplicities and exceptional parameter values require explicit handling.
status: As of 10 November 2026: an established exactly solvable family, already called solved by Baxter in the notebook. The 1971 announcement is verified \citep{baxter1971eight}; the 1973 eigenvector article is bibliographically identified but its direct URL remained inaccessible \citep{baxter1973eigenvectors}. No all-exceptional-parameter completeness theorem is asserted from inaccessible text.

title: Hexagonal closure and parallelizability of planar three-webs
statement: For a regular holomorphic planar three-web, is local equivalence to the three parallel foliations \(x,y,x+y=\mathrm{const}\) equivalent to closure of every sufficiently small web hexagon? Yes: Thomsen's theorem; equivalently the web curvature vanishes.
status: As of 10 November 2026: solved before the seminar (Thomsen, 1927), as recalled in \citet[Sec.~1]{beauville1980tissus}. General three-web linearizability is a different question.

title: Algebraization of maximal-rank codimension-one webs in dimension at least three
statement: For a germ of a regular holomorphic codimension-one \(d\)-web on \(\mathbb C^n\), with every at-most-\(n\) subset of conormals independent, \(n\ge3\), \(d\ge2n\), and rank \(\pi(n,d)\), must the web be locally biholomorphic to the dual web of a projective degree-\(d\) curve?
status: As of 10 November 2026: yes. The 1978 Chern--Griffiths proof had two defects; their 1981 correction added normality. Tr\'epreau, Theorem~1.1, removes that extra condition: preprint first posted 4 August 2005, published 2006. His Theorem~2.4 gives a stronger first-jet criterion. The notebook's theorem is thus solved, not an open problem.
